title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Syrah
objectives: Serve it at the right temperature

steps.title: Meat and spice
steps.body: Syrah's dark fruit and pepper suit grilled and roasted meat: lamb, beef, game and barbecue. Peppery Rhône styles match herbs and black pepper crust. Ripe Barossa Shiraz handles sweet, smoky barbecue sauces. Avoid very delicate dishes, which it overwhelms.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 16 to 18 degrees. Young, powerful Syrah benefits from decanting. Good Hermitage and Côte-Rôtie age 15 to 30 years, developing leather, game and earthy notes. Top Barossa Shiraz also ages well. Simpler Shiraz is best within a few years.

steps.prompt: Which dish suits a peppery northern Rhône Syrah?
options: Lamb with rosemary and black pepper
steps.explanation: Herbs and pepper echo the wine's own aromas; lamb's fat softens its tannins.

steps.title: Beyond the classic
steps.body: Syrah also makes rosé, sparkling red Shiraz, a beloved Australian Christmas wine, and fortified styles in Australia. In blends, it's part of Côtes du Rhône and Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Learning to taste for its pepper is one of the most useful skills in blind tasting.

steps.prompt: Sparkling red Shiraz is a traditional Australian style.
steps.explanation: Yes. It's often served with Christmas lunch in Australia.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Syrah suits lamb, game and barbecue
Serve at 16 to 18 degrees; the best age for decades
It also makes rosé and sparkling red Shiraz
